summary: Remote-controlled PTY shell and filesystem/self-update backdoor driven by WebSocket messages
details: The agent connects to a configured WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages to privileged local handlers. On `terminal_create`, it spawns a PTY (bash/powershell/cmd) on the host via @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch; on `terminal_input`, bytes received from the remote peer are written directly into that PTY's stdin, giving the remote peer arbitrary command execution on the installer's machine. The same message router also handles server-initiated `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `git_push`, `restart_agent`, and `upgrade_agent`. `upgrade_agent` executes `npm install <pkg>@latest` against the configured registry and respawns the agent via systemd/launchd/pm2, allowing the remote peer to swap the running package version. Combined, the WebSocket peer holds full host-level RCE plus workspace, git, and package-update control.
